title: Choosing an indicator

draft.title: Choosing an indicator
card: An indicator is a weak acid or base whose colour changes over a small pH range. The point where it changes colour is the end point.
The equivalence point is where the acid and base have reacted in exact mole ratio. The pH there depends on the salt formed, so it is not always 7.
Strong acid with strong base: pH 7 at equivalence. Strong acid with weak base: below 7, as the salt's cation is a weak acid. Weak acid with strong base: above 7, as the salt's anion is a weak base.

Choose an indicator whose colour change range includes the pH at the equivalence point. Then the end point is very close to the equivalence point. For example, phenolphthalein changes colour at about pH 8 to 10, and methyl orange at about pH 3 to 4.
draft.remember: Match the indicator's colour change range to the pH at the equivalence point.

a.q: Why is the choice of indicator important in a titration?
opts: Its colour change must occur near the equivalence point
It must change colour at exactly pH 7 in every titration
It must react with the acid before the base is added
It must be a stronger acid than the acid being titrated
a.why: The end point only shows when the equivalence point is reached if the colour change happens near it. The equivalence point is not always at pH 7, so an indicator that changes at exactly pH 7 is not needed in every titration.
a.clue: What must the colour change tell you about the reaction?

b.q: Ethanoic acid, a weak acid, is titrated with sodium hydroxide, a strong base. Which indicator is the best choice?
opts: Phenolphthalein, which changes at about pH 8 to 10
Methyl orange, which changes at about pH 3 to 4
Either one, because the titration involves a strong base
Neither one, because the equivalence point is at pH 7
b.why: The salt formed has an anion that is a weak base, so the pH at equivalence is above 7. Phenolphthalein changes colour in that range. Methyl orange changes well below it, so it would show an end point long before the equivalence point.
b.clue: Is the pH at equivalence above, below or at 7 for a weak acid and strong base?

a.best: Its colour change must occur near the equivalence point

b.best: Phenolphthalein, which changes at about pH 8 to 10
